entries.title: Clearer help, richer cases and three practical improvements
entries.summary: A standardized opening five, varied everyday negotiations, concise scoped help, a focused performance review and mobile controls that stay reachable.

Participant experience: Responsive chat and six-issue offers, inline mobile Neggy, editable public-ready drafts and explicit review of ambiguous proposals.
The feedback review now leads with three priorities, numbered steps and saved evidence. Smaller ideas and supporting graphs open when needed.
The two leading dashboard boxes are Top 3 improvements and AI-use tips, above historical performance.
Outdated saved reviews are flagged, with a free method-update replacement. The normal five-round refresh count remains explicit. Red review-date markers are reconstructed on earlier score histories.
Research mechanics: Fixed opening case IDs saved per treatment; Mixed default, then random allowed-pool return rounds.
Ten active four-to-six-issue integrative cases, plus twelve distributive cases; exact finite ZOPA and score calibration retained privately.
AI architecture: Three scope-based suggestions, preflight/output/execution gates, message-only assessments and fifty-word private advice fallback.
Collaborative/balanced/firm own-value negotiation policies; safeguards prevent ideal-package resets and extra concessions for repetition.
Data and audit: AI-copy versus official AI-sent offer provenance, exact issue terms, case diagnostics, review planning and correction events.
Five-category QA register, comprehensive checklist, case audit and methods addendum.

validation: The full regression suite and TypeScript pass; the final test count is retained in Arena_v33_All_Tests.log and the packaging receipt.
One synthetic five-round HTTP sequence passed all 55 operations, scored 180 total and 36 average, with zero model calls.
Targeted live helper/counterpart/review probes retained raw results, failures and corrections. The final feedback sample produced three priorities and four smaller ideas in one call.
Responsive visual and interaction checks are recorded in Arena_v33_UX_QA.json with explicit verification limits.
limits: Equal payoff maxima do not establish equal task difficulty or bargaining-strength reliability.
Fixed case order ties case and task type to position in the mixed sequence. Self-selected delegation is observational.
No new live concurrent-user capacity claim; most checks ran locally. Paid recruitment still needs the approved consent/payment configuration.

Use a separate full-width signed-score row and the short empty state Choose terms.

Visual.fix: Reconstruct dated red markers from saved review coverage and creation metadata without changing old scores.
Visual.checked: Two saved review dates yielded grouped markers in dashboard and report graphs; old-data count fallback tested.

Content.checked: Own-role case audit; actual job preparation and development UI read.

entries.title: A quick reminder of who Neggy is
entries.summary: The support-choice heading introduces Neggy as your AI assistant, and the three options explicitly name Neggy the AI.

Clearer signposts: The next-round introduction briefly identifies Neggy as your AI assistant.
Preparation, live coaching and negotiation choices explicitly name Neggy the AI.
Offer permissions, check-in settings and negotiation status use Neggy consistently.
Existing assistant headers retain Your AI Negotiation Assistant. The reminder appears in the heading, without another explanatory text block.

validation: TypeScript and the production build are checked before publication. No model calls are needed for these interface wording changes.
limits: This release changes interface wording; saved AI permissions, prompts and scored outcomes remain as recorded.

entries.title: Neggy joins your corner
entries.summary: A professional, friendly assistant now guides the warm-up and keeps help close throughout the negotiation.

Meet Neggy: Neggy has a more professional face, navy glasses and six expressions. The subtitle is Your AI Negotiation Assistant.
The larger floating cloud can be dragged, remembers its browser position and stays within the screen after resizing. Clicking or pressing Enter opens the docked helper.
The window can be minimized, restored and enlarged. The mobile dialog has one visible header. Reduced-motion preferences stop the decorative animation.
A guided first negotiation: Neggy introduces the warm-up, preparation, four lessons and the transition into scored play. Each lesson has one short instruction and an example when useful.
The four motions remain: send a structured offer, send an ordinary message, make an offer in chat and ask for private advice. Actual progress, early exits and permanent skipping remain distinct.
Tutorial confirmations are marked as private Neggy messages in chat exports and excluded from the counterpart prompt. These scripted instructions add no model requests.
The guide has a separate version. Completed steps are retained for returning players; changing the companion does not make them repeat the tutorial.
Advice with a clear voice: The editable Neggy voice module applies only to private helper roles. The counterpart keeps its separate instructions.
Neggy is warm and direct, with short bullets, plain language and concrete next steps. Humour is occasional and never forced.
Preparation builds on the player’s answer. Own-role preferences do not establish the other side’s priorities; the prompt now asks the helper to test that assumption.
Scoring remains deterministic. Neggy receives own-role material and authorized history, with verified value placeholders. No-help rounds have no helper window or launcher.
A clearer negotiation screen: The negotiation number is larger and highlighted. Session time and negotiation time are centered, use distinct colours and become urgent as configured time runs out.
One sentence identifies the player’s role, fee direction and named partner. End negotiation sits on the right.
Own proposals and own point strips share orange styling; the other side uses blue. Positive offer values include a plus sign.
Steering options are visible before the first instruction. A selected approach appears in private history with Neggy’s acknowledgement.
Release checks: The bounded leaderboard refresh filters out load-test accounts before choosing its next page. It refreshes derived standings without rewriting negotiations or paid awards.
Admin password sessions are verified against the configured researcher on both hosts. A private-host bypass alone does not grant researcher access.

validation: 304 application tests and TypeScript passed before the final release build.
A complete local browser tutorial included a structured offer, ordinary chat, the mistyped offer I can offerr 1.35k, private advice and progression into scored play.

Browser checks covered dragging without opening, position persistence after reload, bounds at 390 pixels, the mobile window, a 1920-pixel workspace, enlargement, steering acknowledgement and no-helper mode.

Four small real-model voice probes were retained, including the initial preparation reply that was too long. After revision, preparation replies were 64 and 63 words. These checks do not establish general model reliability.
limits: Public and private publication are tracked separately. Check the release receipt for the deployment status and configuration applied to each host.
A companion can affect perceived agency and subjective value. Keep interaction and tutorial-guide versions in analysis; do not interpret a presentation change as constant fidelity.
The companion does not expand scope, authority or the permitted number of AI offers. Existing study prompt snapshots stay frozen.

entries.title: A shared Arena and clearer control
entries.summary: We reviewed the November 10 chats, repaired missed replies and a changed-price acceptance error, and made AI authority and check-ins explicit.

One Arena leaderboard: Shared profiles appear together across task types, prompt versions, backends and historical scoring scales. New profiles appear as New until they finish a scored negotiation.
Each profile has one entry. Average points rank first; total points break ties. Opt-outs are respected. Financial study ranks remain separate.
A bounded admin refresh rebuilds derived entries from saved histories. Negotiations, original points and paid awards are never rewritten.
Reliable conversation: Reject, decline a proposed final deal and reopen an accepted deal now receive a counterpart response.
The observed “Ok 1100” error is fixed: a changed amount is a counteroffer, not acceptance of a different standing price.
Starting point and at this point no longer trigger the private-score guard. Actual point disclosures remain guarded.
An unsupported claim about an earlier offer is corrected and logged. The counterpart prompt now explicitly separates each party’s offer history.
Scope, authority and check-ins: Live coaching includes preparation and two concise scope groups. Scope and offer-sending choices begin unanswered.
Negotiator offer authority and final-deal authority use separate, explicit two-sided controls. Start stays disabled until every required choice is made.
Players choose a pause after 1, 2, 3 or 5 sent AI offers, or Until I pause. Questions do not consume a new offer checkpoint. Approvals, Pause and deadlines still apply.
The contract, cadence unit, change reason and subsequent continuation decisions are logged. Old active rounds retain their earlier two-action policy.
Preparation and detailed feedback: Preparation opens with a role-specific question without a model call. Follow-up help is conversational, concise and saved privately.
The first detailed performance review requires five scored negotiations. Each update requires five new negotiations. Saved reviews remain available.
Reviews use themed action cards, brief examples and verified score facts. A completed but invalid review can receive one audited validation repair; network errors do not trigger hidden retries.
Tutorial and navigation: Skip tutorial is prominent before and during the warm-up. Each confirmation starts a visible six-second countdown enforced on the server.
A skipped tutorial is permanently unavailable on that profile. Skipped exposure and genuinely completed lessons remain distinguishable.
Named partner, role and fee direction are visible. Round, preparation, chat, final-decision and result transitions have short dialogs.
Waiting at a new-round entry dialog does not consume the negotiation timer; the Prolific visit deadline continues.
Layout and profiles: The negotiation workspace fills wide displays. Role text and scoring references are larger; the conversation and helper use defined panels.
Steering presets collapse so custom instructions stay visible. Mobile score-header overflow is repaired.
The saved-profile picker supports search and more remembered profiles. Admin sign-in no longer changes the participant persona on public routes.
New unpaid return rounds receive current prompt improvements while preserving their inherited economic rules. Active study visits keep their frozen prompt policy.

validation: Fresh application regression suite and TypeScript checks are required before packaging.
Local browser walkthroughs cover a full tutorial, profile switching, review gating, explicit authority, offer checkpoints and the six-second skip.
Targeted live Luna checks and their raw validation results are retained in the v31 release evidence.
limits: This is targeted release validation, not a general model reliability estimate.
Historical pilot point scales are kept as earned on the shared social board. Current calibrated study analyses must filter by scoring version.
Paid recruitment remains pending the protocol and study-specific launch configuration.

entries.title: Advice that protects your current offer
entries.summary: A live warm-up check exposed a worse-price draft hiding inside a message. It now goes through the same exact-value checks as a structured suggestion.

Coach checks: Price-bearing private drafts become explicit validated packages before they can be copied or sent.
A counteroffer worse than the available package is replaced with a computed reciprocal candidate using only the player’s own values and public offers.
If numeric prose is rejected, the player gets concrete verified terms and a useful next step instead of a generic instruction to read the point sheet.
Guarded model responses remain distinguishable from raw model output in the researcher audit.

validation: The actual observed live response is replayed against the fix, alongside role, score, scope and privacy regressions.
Final checks and live examples are recorded in the v30.1 release receipt.
limits: Computed suggestions do not establish that the other side will accept.
This repair does not validate a model’s general negotiation competence.

entries.title: A simpler start, with fewer ways to get stuck
entries.summary: A price-only warm-up, clearer offer recovery and matched score opportunities.

Getting started: The first lesson is a structured price offer, visible before the chat composer. Examples guide the chat, typed offer and helper steps.
Finish warm-up stays visible. Old stalled attempts can continue or restart without losing their transcript. Skipped lessons are recorded honestly.
A predictable teaching counterpart counters an ambitious opening, holds against repetition and worse prices, and leaves the player free to finish.
Offers and points: A source-first natural-language interpreter separates meaning from exact score calculation. Clear numeric offers remain fast.
Missing terms open as blank highlighted choices beside the editable original message. Unsupported conditions do not acquire silent defaults.
Semantic or helper outages have a safe review/example path. Ordinary amount-free questions do not need an interpretation model.
Comparable opportunities: New main rules give both roles and both forms a 100-point legal ceiling, zero for no deal, negative possibilities and a matched 72-point best mutually acceptable score.
The twenty main stories are audited, including the limited diversity of the integrative issue skeleton. Historical rules and paid terms are retained.
Training exposure, interpreter prompt hashes and usage are recorded separately from coaching. The new prompt is editable in admin.

validation: All application regression results, local state-machine stress and browser walkthroughs are retained in the v30 release receipt.
The repaired 49-case saved-output suite and 15 fresh targeted probes passed. Initial misses and the model timeout remain in the audit.
Local stress covered 3,600 deterministic offer variants, 80 negotiations, 590 offers and 60 final-decision checks without hosted load.
limits: These checks do not establish population reliability, equal empirical case difficulty or live-model capacity.
The twenty main stories do not represent twenty different issue families.
The legal ceiling is not a promise that the other side will accept a one-sided maximum. Paid recruitment remains off.

entries.title: More room for your next move
entries.summary: A clearer workspace, marked sliders, private AI guidance and an average-first leaderboard.

The experience: The negotiation workspace uses the available desktop width. Role & Points and Notes share a left panel; chat remains above a compact inline offer.
A marked native seven-point slider replaces the previous button scale. Next-round reflections show and enforce a 30-character minimum.
Home features the leaderboard and a clear new-player action. Returning players can spot public nicknames beside their saved profiles.
The default desktop cursor uses the Arena logo while interactive controls keep their usual cursor.
Your AI and agreements: Specific theory-informed steering presets and custom instructions are saved as private chat, followed by a concise acknowledgement without an extra API request.
When a counterpart accepts your offer, review the exact terms and points before finalizing or continuing. A pending accepted package finalizes if its deadline ends first.
The outcome recap identifies proposal, acceptance and finalization. New Yes/No questions record perceived ability to do better after official AI offers or AI agreement.
Progress and rankings: Average points set the main live rank; total points break tied averages. A separate total-points view remains available.
Future v6 paid-visit prizes use average then total. Older saved policies and finalized payments are preserved.
The dashboard features play, feedback access, clearly labeled warmth/competence axes, detailed-history buttons, return-link copying and friend challenges.
Researcher reference: A searchable private Game mechanics tab documents 20 parts of the experience, data and source files. The full guide is also saved locally.

New guidance, provisional-deal, finalization and perceived-AI comparison events remain in researcher exports. Optional board exposures are timestamped as observations; they never count as generated reviews. The comparison question’s position before SVI is documented as a potential source of priming.

validation: 246 application tests passed before final visual review, including provisional agreement, deadline, private-steering, average-ranking, legacy-award and profile-isolation regressions.
TypeScript passed. Desktop, mobile and hosted publication receipts are recorded separately.
The current development checks use policy fixtures and deterministic acknowledgements; no paid model calls are needed for the repair.
limits: Communication indicators remain exploratory wording signals, not validated traits or ability.
The new perceived-AI comparison can affect subsequent SVI responses; retain its administration version.
Email sending, physical-phone keyboard checks and a 100-user simultaneous live-AI capacity certification remain outside this patch.

entries.title: Come back to your Arena
entries.summary: A clear Home screen, one entry choice and an easy way to find saved profiles.

Returning players: Find my profile is visible on the new-player Home screen. A remembered player gets Continue as their profile name and Choose a saved profile.
Profiles made in earlier preview links can be selected from the same browser. Selecting one returns to the main address with its own saved progress.
New profiles are remembered at the main address after creation. Completed tutorials stay complete.
A simpler start: General User and Prolific Participant are one selector. Selecting a type changes one next-step button rather than launching setup immediately.
Prolific study links still enter the linked study directly. The ordinary Home screen explains where to use a Prolific study link.
On a phone, the entry card comes before the introduction so the main actions appear early.
Home and saved work: The named Home button and Arena logo open the landing screen from setup or a negotiation. They retain the current preview scope.
An unsent chat draft, private notes and unfinished round ratings remain in the same tab when navigating Home and returning.
Leaving an active negotiation does not stop its clock. Home shows a short reminder.
The final study check-in retains its deadline behavior. Account selection clears a stale launch cookie without editing study records.
Access: Same-browser choices require the existing browser cookie. A claimed nickname or Prolific ID cannot disclose another profile.
Profile name and PIN remain available for another device. Unconfigured email sign-in stays hidden.

validation: 234 application tests and TypeScript passed before packaging; the production build is recorded in the deployment receipt.
A local HTTP check verified profile listing, exact-profile resumption, completed tutorial preservation, new-profile memory and rejected cross-origin or other-browser access.
Browser checks covered both audience choices, Home from the plan and consent, saved-profile selection through the first scored negotiation, retained chat and notes, and a 390-pixel phone layout.
No model calls were needed for this navigation repair.
limits: A different browser needs the previously configured PIN or a verified email once email delivery is configured. A profile name by itself is not proof of access.
The active clock continues on Home. Same-tab unsent drafts do not promise recovery after the tab is closed.

entries.title: A tutorial that understands your offers
entries.summary: Typos, ordinary phrasing and pasted offers can make progress without repeated notices.

Chat offers: Recognizes the reported would-like-to-pay and Okay-so offers, common setup/payment misspellings and multiline pasted terms. Numbers are parsed exactly and points stay deterministic.
Ambiguous terms stay uncommitted. Review the terms restores the exact sent text to the editable composer, with no guessed package.
Use this example inserts a valid opening for editing. Short questions such as like what count as conversation.
Tutorial progress: Each demonstrated chat, conversation and structured-offer action is credited once. Extra offers do not trigger a sequencing error.
Affected old tutorials recover lesson credit from saved attempts without rewriting historical messages, offers or scores.
If that affected attempt already timed out, one unscored recovery attempt resumes its remaining steps. New tutorials keep the existing time cap.
Conversation clarity: System notices use pink boxes and italic body text, distinct from either party. The review action shares the existing notice rather than duplicating it.
The warm-up supplier answers questions about its own priorities and varies its replies. Repeated identical offers still earn no extra concession.
The required-helper completion notice appears once.

validation: Exact reported messages plus typo, multiline, ambiguous and quoted/conditional regression cases.
Browser replay covered draft restoration, a single pink notice, typo offer scoring, a short reply, the offer form, one live helper request and entry to the first scored negotiation.
A separate expired legacy fixture recovered its first two actions and resumed at the offer box. Final checks and host receipts are stored separately.
limits: The recognizer tolerates a bounded issue vocabulary; uncertain or conflicting terms are left editable rather than guessed.
The warm-up uses scripted policy before the required helper. This check is not an expert-quality certification of all advice.

entries.title: A clearer profile and visible PIN entry
entries.summary: A simpler gender menu and an easy-to-see PIN field.

Your profile: Gender choices are Man, Woman and Other identity. Previously saved identities remain intact.
New PINs are visible while being created, with a clear Show PIN / Hide PIN button.
The PIN field has a white background, blue border, six-digit hint, larger numbers and an obvious focus state.

validation: TypeScript/build and focused browser checks recorded in the v28.1 release receipt.
limits: This update does not change stored PIN hashes or negotiation behavior.

entries.title: Hands-on practice, deliberate AI choices and saved feedback
entries.summary: Try the controls once, choose your AI support afresh, and build on saved performance feedback.

First-time practice: Four guided steps cover a typed offer, a persuasive non-offer reply, the offer box and private AI help.
Completed profiles keep their tutorial status. Early acceptance cannot silently skip the lesson; the time limit still has a final-decision route.
Your feedback: Communication plots use participant-sent wording, exclude AI-sent offers and show insufficient-data guidance. The indicators are exploratory, with their calculation disclosed.
An optional detailed review unlocks after a scored round and saves to the profile. Another requires five new completed negotiations.
Reviews cite saved messages and cases. Scores, charts and term-value statements come from the deterministic own-role calculations.
Research and operations: The reviewer has an editable named prompt and a separate validated report schema. No profile, private notes, questionnaire answers or opponent payoff table is sent.
Review views and communication-panel exposure enter the research export. They remain observational feedback interventions, not validated trait measurements.
Usage is metered separately for the dashboard reviewer. Requests are idempotent and the server prevents concurrent or early repeat reviews.
Choice-policy metadata distinguishes manual selections from separately assigned experimental conditions.
Your AI choice: No AI role, coaching scope or decision permission is preselected in free-choice rounds. A blue Last time marker shows the previous setup without selecting it.
A short question appears only if the role, scope or either decision permission changes. The answer is saved for research and never enters the AI context.
The same rule applies to optional negotiations. Unchanged reselections and the first scored choice do not trigger the question.

validation: 226 local application checks passed; final TypeScript/build and publication evidence are recorded in the release receipt.
The four-step tutorial and saved-profile return behavior passed local UI/API checks.
A synthetic five-round history exercised review persistence, response reuse and the five-new-round gate. The corrected review-v3 used deterministic case facts and passed its live check.
An earlier timeout, an overstrict number-word filter, excessive evidence references and a qualitative term-value misstatement were retained and corrected.

A local browser walkthrough verified blank choices, the previous-choice marker, change explanation, cancellation and two-action AI renewal with private steering. No model calls were needed for that fixture.

The public host completed a 51-request smoke journey through the four tutorial actions, five cases, an optional sixth, both roles, changed-choice explanation, scheduled SVI and completion. The private host and stored prompt pack were checked in admin.
limits: Communication indicators need human validation and are not personality or ability scores.
A small synthetic review check does not establish expert-level advice. Physical-device keyboard testing and 100-person live-AI capacity are not certified.
Real paid recruitment stays off until the study-specific release requirements are configured.

entries.title: A clearer round, from preparation to the next challenge
entries.summary: Clearer stage changes, a roomier conversation and renewed control over AI-led negotiation.

Participant flow: Short preparation, negotiation, final-decision and result dialogs make stage changes clear.
Five completed rounds open the choice to continue; the closing survey appears when the player finishes.
Scores and average are more prominent. Each result can show an earned rank update.
Negotiation workspace: Role and points stay on the left, conversation in the centre and support on the right on wide screens.
Message entry is above the official offer. The offer starts empty, shows its range and glows blue until first use.
Chat has no global move limit within the time window. The final minute permits one counteroffer.
AI support: One page separates preparation, coaching and negotiation, with independent offer and deal permissions.
AI-led play runs in two-action batches and accepts private steering.
Shorter, concrete advice uses the player's role material and verified calculations.
Balanced counterpart thresholds address an overly rigid final threshold while keeping repeated-offer protections.
Research and operations: New rank snapshots separate live encouragement from paid-study award calculations.
Current public-name consent controls whether screen names are shown. Earlier private names retain aliases.
Admin gains a password shortcut and this versioned update log.
A portable design and Cloudflare handoff ZIP records the owner's aesthetic and writing preferences.

validation: 213 local application checks and 11 analysis/export checks passed. TypeScript passed.

Local browser checks covered preparation and early entry, the practice helper gate, negative agreement, final counteroffer, reflection and rank order, shorthand offers, draft retention and cancelling the end countdown.
Phone 390×844 and tablet 900×900 viewport checks passed without horizontal overflow. These are responsive-browser checks, not physical-device keyboard tests.

Twenty targeted live model calls across two prompt versions cost USD 0.00954764. The final preparation prompt passed two probes without numerical quarantine. Earlier quarantines and qualitative limits are recorded.
A local six-round HTTP journey completed five assigned cases, an optional sixth, scheduled SVI and the final survey. Hosted smoke results are retained in the release receipt.
limits: Real paid recruitment stays off until study-specific ethics and recruitment settings are configured.
Small model probes do not establish expert-level bargaining. Live-AI capacity at 100 simultaneous users has not been demonstrated.
This timestamp records the implemented source. The separate deployment receipt records each host’s publication time and source commit.

entries.title: Zero-point no-deal scores and concrete own-role advice
entries.summary: No agreement now earns zero, while deliberately accepting a poor deal can earn negative points. Advice and scoring use distinct responsibilities.

Points and instructions: The score origin moved to the outside option without changing the underlying zone of possible agreement.
The participant's role, fee direction and scored terms are clearer.
Historical sessions retain their saved rules and end-of-round metrics.
Model reliability: Preparation computes role-specific targets, limits and trade costs.
Unsupported numerical advice is quarantined instead of being presented as fact.
A public daily AI allowance is reserved atomically before calls.
Access: The public Cloudflare app and owner-only private mirror were checked.
Nickname and PIN sign-in support returning profiles.

validation: 198 application checks and 10 analysis-data checks passed.
Local and hosted five-negotiation smoke journeys were completed.
Small model prompt evaluations were recorded in the quality and cost evidence.
limits: This entry was reconstructed from retained release evidence. The day is recorded; an exact publication time has not been inferred.
A separate historical 100-user synthetic test made zero model calls and does not establish real-model capacity.
